sentences.text: Kunpengornis is an extinct genus of euornithean birds.
The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered by a farmer near Lamadong in Jianchang County, Liaoning Province, China.
The farmer who found the fossil donated it to the Anhui Geological Museum in 2023.
The genus name combines the mythical Chinese Kunpeng with the Greek word for bird, while the species name anhuimusei honors the museum holding the holotype.
Fish bones found in its abdominal cavity indicate that Kunpengornis was a fish-eater.
Kunpengornis is the genus name for this extinct bird, with the only known species being Kunpengornis anhuimusei, a genus established by Huang et al. in 2026.
Phylogenetic analyses place Kunpengornis within Euornithes as the sister taxon to Piscivoravis, having diverged after the Yanornithidae but before the Gansuidae and Ornithuromorpha.
Kunpengornis is classified under the class Reptilia.
Kunpengornis lived during the Early Cretaceous (Aptian age) in Liaoning Province, China, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
